POSTS.title: How to Rank Higher on Google Maps in 2026
POSTS.ex: A step-by-step guide to optimising your Google Business Profile so local customers find you first.
body: When someone searches for a service near them, Google shows three businesses in the Map Pack before any website. Getting into those three spots is the fastest way for a local business to win more calls.
Your primary category is the strongest ranking signal on your profile. Pick the most specific one that describes your main service, then add secondary categories for everything else you offer.
Your business name, address and phone number must match on your website, your profile and every directory. Even small differences like 'Rd' and 'Road' can confuse Google.
3. Post every week and reply to every review
Share an offer, update or project photo every week
Reply to every review within 48 hours
Add new photos of your real work each month
Do these three things consistently for two months and most businesses see a clear rise in Maps visibility.

POSTS.title: How Much Does a Small Business Website Cost in the UK?
POSTS.ex: What you should expect to pay for a website in 2026, and what is worth paying extra for.
body: Website prices in the UK range from a few hundred pounds to tens of thousands. The difference usually comes down to three things: how many pages you need, how custom the design is, and what the site needs to do.
Number of pages and amount of content
Features like booking, shop or member areas
For most small service businesses a professional 5 to 12 page website costs between £700 and £1,500. Online stores and custom features cost more.
Speed, mobile layout and basic SEO are not optional extras. A cheap site that loads slowly and does not rank will cost you more in lost enquiries than you saved.

POSTS.title: Google Ads for Local Businesses: A Beginner's Guide
POSTS.ex: Set up your first campaign without wasting budget on the wrong clicks.
body: Google Ads can bring enquiries within days, but a poorly set up campaign can spend your budget on people who were never going to buy.
Search campaigns show your ad when someone types a specific query. They are the most predictable place to start for local service businesses.
Negative keywords added for jobs, free and DIY searches
Conversion tracking on calls and forms before launch
Review your search terms report every week and add negatives. This one habit usually cuts wasted spend by 20 to 30 percent.

POSTS.title: Why Google Reviews Matter More Than Ever
POSTS.ex: How reviews affect your ranking and conversions, and the simple system to collect more.
body: Reviews influence both where you rank and whether people choose you. A business with 80 reviews at 4.8 stars will usually beat one with 10 reviews at 5 stars.
The best time to ask is straight after a job is finished and the customer is happy. Send a short text with a direct link to your review form.
Replies show future customers that you care. Thank happy customers by name, and answer unhappy ones calmly with an offer to put things right.

POSTS.title: 5 Social Media Ideas for Local Businesses
POSTS.ex: Simple post ideas that build trust and bring in local customers without hours of work.
body: You do not need to go viral to win customers from social media. You need to show up regularly and show real people doing real work.
Before and after photos of your work
A short video introducing a team member
Answers to questions customers often ask
Behind the scenes on a busy day
Post three times a week, reply to every comment, and you will build a local audience that remembers you when they need you.

POSTS.title: Does Your Small Business Really Need Branding?
POSTS.ex: Why a consistent look helps customers trust you, and where to start on a small budget.
body: Branding is more than a logo. It is the colours, words and feeling people connect with your business every time they see it.
When your van, website, invoices and social posts all look the same, customers see an established business. When they all look different, they wonder if you are.
A clear logo that works small and large
One or two fonts used everywhere
Start with these and apply them everywhere. You can grow into a full brand guide later.
